- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after initial spikes.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the 30-day window, particularly after mid-range peaks.
- Strong mean reversion bias: forecasts often fail to account for price correction after sharp rises.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — underreacts to downward momentum.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in high-volatility periods, failing to capture downward pressure from supply/demand shocks.
- Model tends to ignore recent low-price trends when forecasting, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are systematically too high, especially when recent prices are falling.
